BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r1.claim: Every soul, whether human or otherwise, is included; the generic indefinite noun is valid because it conveys universality.
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r1.anchor: من النفوس سواء كان نفس الإنسان أو غيرها وهو مبتدأ وجاز الابتداء بالنكرة

BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r2.claim: Tasting death means experiencing its bitterness and the pangs of separation; this assumes tasting can refer to little or much.
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r2.anchor: وهذا مبني على أن الذوق يصلح للقليل والكثير كما ذهب إليه الراغب

BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r3.claim: Another view takes tasting literally as a small amount taken by mouth: souls undergo a portion of death through contact with the body.
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r3.anchor: أصل الذوق بالفم فيما يقل تناوله فالمعنى

BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r4.claim: A human consists of body, soul, and a subtle vapor between them called the animal spirit; life continues while this connection remains viable, then ends when it extinguishes and the soul involuntarily leaves the body, a formal death.
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أن الإنسان روحا وجسدا وبخارا لطيفا بينهما هو الروح الحيواني

BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r5.claim: Only those who have fully disengaged from ordinary attachment know how the spirit appears in the body and departs at death.
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r5.anchor: ولا يعرف كيفية ظهور الروح في البدن ومفارقته له وقت الموت إلا أهل الانسلاخ التام

BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#2/r6.claim: Returning to God means returning to His judgment and recompense.

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r1.claim: Turja'un derives from raj' and means that you are returned.
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r1.anchor: {ترجعون} من الرجع وهو الرد أي تردون

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r2.claim: Since this is the final outcome, people should prepare for it and regard leaving home and exile as easy when their homeland is a land of idolatry or sin and innovation they cannot change; they should migrate to a land of obedience.
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r2.anchor: فمن كانت هذه عاقبته ينبغي أن يجتهد في التزود والاستعداد لها

SULAMI:v2p119/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p119/r1.claim: The self dies when the Real's witnessing effaces its independent selfhood; God revives it through witnessing Him, removes its defects, and establishes it in truth.
SULAMI:v2p119/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : النفوس وإن عظم خطرها فإنها مردودة إلى قيمتها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r1.claim: Ali reports that after the Prophet died, an unseen visitor came to console the Prophet's family; the visitor said every soul dies, God comforts those struck by calamity, and true loss is being deprived of reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r1.anchor: ان علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه ، قال لما توفي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجاءت التعزية فجاهم ات يسمعون حسه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r2.claim: Ali identifies the unseen visitor who offered condolences as al-Khidr.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r2.anchor: قال جعفر بن محمد اخبرني أبي ان علي بن أبي طالب قال : تدرون من هذا ؟ هذا الخضر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r3.claim: Ali reports the visitor's condolence that God is consolation for every calamity and replacement for what is lost, and that the true bereaved person is deprived of reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3076/r3.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ان في الله عزاء من كل مصيبة ، وخلفا من كل ما فات فبالله فثقوا واياه فارجوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p22/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p22/r6.claim: The death verse is a second interruption between the two clauses, strengthening their warning and promise, easing persecution even unto death by recalling eternal reward, and hinting at future jihad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p22/r6.anchor: اعتراض ثان بين الجملتين المتعاطفتين قصد منها تأكيد الوعيد الذي تضمنته جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r7.claim: The certainty of death and return diminishes worldly fears of emigration, such as dying or going hungry, and urges prompt obedience and migration to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r7.anchor: تحقير لأمر الدنيا ومخاوفها كأن بعض المؤمنين نظر في عاقبة تلحقه في خروجه من وطنه أنه يموت أو يجوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r8.claim: Most read tarjiʿūn with second-person tāʾ; a yāʾ reading is reported from ʿAsim and Abu Hatim from Abu ʿAmr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ترجعون» بالتاء من فوق، ورويت عن عاصم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r9.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r9.claim: Abu Haywa reads kullu nafsin dhāʾiqatun al-mawta, with tanwīn on dhāʾiqa and accusative mawta.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «كل نفس ذائقة» بالتنوين «الموت»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r1.claim: The reminder that every soul dies makes migration from the abode of unbelief easier to bear; after death people return to God for recompense according to their deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r1.anchor: ثم خوفهم بالموت لتهون عليهم الهجرة فقال كل نفس ذائقة الموت المعنى فلا تقيموا في دار الشرك خوفا من الموت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r2.claim: Most readers use the second-person plural form of “you will be returned.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r2.anchor: والأكثرون قرؤوا ترجعون بالتاء على الخطاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r3.claim: Abū Bakr, transmitting from ʿĀṣim, reads the verb in the third person with yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p281#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم بالياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r3.claim: Oppressed Muslims migrated first to Abyssinia, where the Negus sheltered them, then the Prophet and the remaining Companions migrated to Medina; death catches everyone, so obey God wherever He directs and expect the return to Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r3.anchor: خرجوا مهاجرين إلى أرض الحبشة، ليأمنوا، على دينهم هناك

JISHUMI:v8p5586/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r5.speaker: عاصم
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r5.claim: In one transmission, ʿĀṣim reads “you are returned” with yāʾ referring to everyone; the other readers use the second-person tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r5.anchor: قرأ عاصم في بعض الروايات عنه: يرجعون بالياء إلى الكل

JISHUMI:v8p5587/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r4.claim: “Tasting death” is read in the genitive construction, though a non-construct reading is also possible; “ka-ʾayyin” means “how many.”
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r4.anchor: (ذائقة الموت) جر على الإضافة، ويجوز لغير الإضافة

JISHUMI:v8p5587/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r12.claim: Every living person dies wherever they are, so believers should not remain in a land of polytheism; they return to God for resurrection and recompense.
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r12.anchor: كل حي يموت يناله الموت بأي أرض كان، فلا تقيموا بأرض الشرك

JISHUMI:v8p5587/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r13.claim: Alternatively, this teaches that the world is a transient waystation and should not be preferred over the everlasting abode of the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v8p5587/r13.anchor: دار الدنيا دار نقلة، فلا نختارها على دار الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.claim: The death verse follows the command to seek a land suited to worship: everyone will experience death's bitterness and anguish, then reach requital, so one must prepare for it with all one's effort.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت } أي واجدة مرارته وكربه كما يجد الذائق طعم المذوق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r9.claim: Every living being dies; alternatively, every soul experiences death's anguish and severity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r9.anchor: يعني أن كل حي ميت . الثاني : أنها تجد كربه وشدته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r10.claim: Mention of death can frighten people away from sins or prevent them from being misled when a prophet dies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r10.anchor: إرهابا بالموت ليقلعوا عن المعاصي . الثاني : ليعلمهم أن أنبياء الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r11.claim: After Muhammad's death, an unseen caller consoled the Prophet's family: God compensates for every loss, and the deprived person is one deprived of reward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r11.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال لما توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاءهم آت

MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.claim: God reminds migrants that everyone dies and returns for judgment; faithful, righteous migrants receive eternal rooms with rivers, and those patient through migration trust God despite lacking money or livelihood in Medina.
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.anchor: ثم خوفهم الموت ليهاجروا، فقال تعالى: { كل نفس ذآئقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون } [آية: 57]

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r1.claim: Every soul experiences death's bitterness and distress as one tastes food; certainty of death makes leaving one's homeland easier.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r1.anchor: أى واجدة مرارته وكربه كما يجد الذائق طعم المذوق لأنها إذا تيقنت بالموت سهل عليها مفاوقة وطنها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r2.claim: After death people return to God for reward and punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ ثم إلينا ترجعون ﴾ بعد الموت للثوب والعقاب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r3.speaker: يحيى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r3.claim: Yaḥyā reads يرجعون in the passive.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r4.speaker: يعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#4/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb reads ترجعون in the active address form.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r8.claim: The reminder that every soul dies, also discussed in Āl ʿImrān, diminishes worldly fears: believers concerned about death or hunger in leaving Mecca should hasten to obedience and migration.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r8.anchor: وإنما ذكره هاهنا تحقيرا لأمر الدنيا ومخاوفها

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.claim: The Prophet says that one who flees from land to land for the sake of religion, even by a handspan, merits Paradise and the companionship of Muhammad and Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.anchor: من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض ولو قيد شبر استوجب الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.speaker: السلمي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.claim: Al-Sulamī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read yarjiʿūn with yāʾ, matching the preceding mention of every soul tasting death; the other readers use tāʾ, matching the address to believing servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وأبو بكر عن عاصم: { يرجعون } بالياء

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.claim: The cited elegy laments death, warns against attachment to worldly beauty, and asks what became of former loved ones and neighbors.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.anchor: الموت في كل حين ينشد الكفنا ونحن في غفلة عما يراد بنا

SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r1.claim: Abu Bakr reads ترجعون in the third person, as he does at 30:11; Abu Amr agrees there, while the others use second person in both verses.
SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r1.anchor:
قرأه بالغيبة أبو بكر، وكذا في الروم في قوله:
ثم إليه ترجعون

SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:57/r2.claim: A further reading has يرجعون in the active voice.

RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r1.claim: Since migration made believers grieve over leaving home and family, God reminds them that death is inevitable and that dying in His cause earns recompense at their return to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r1.anchor: فقال لهم إن ما تكرهون لا بد من وقوعه فإن كل نفس ذائقة الموت والموت مفرق الأحباب

RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r2.claim: In a subtler reading, the self that remains attached to itself must taste death; it should instead attach to God, since every other thing perishes.
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r2.anchor: فمن يريد ألا يذوق الموت لا يبقى مع نفسه فإن / النفس ذائقته بل يتعلق بغيره

RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r3.claim: Attachment to God makes death a return to Him rather than annihilation, as shown by martyrs’ life with God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r3.anchor: إذا تعلقتم بي فموتكم رجوع إلي وليس بموت

RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r4.claim: A Prophetic saying expresses this reading by saying believers do not die but move from one abode to another.
RAZI-FULL:v25p74#3/r4.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( المؤمنون لا يموتون بل ينقلون من دار إلى دار )

STUDYQURAN:29:57/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:57/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:57/r1.claim: This frequently quoted verse parallels 3:185 and 21:35.

STUDYQURAN:29:57/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:57/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:57/r2.claim: Because death is inevitable, the previous verse’s command to worship God means everyone must prepare for death through worship.
STUDYQURAN:29:57/r2.anchor: In the immediate context, this frequently quoted verse explains why the previous verse enjoins worship of God.

TABATABAI:29:56-59/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r4.claim: The death-and-return reminder reinforces the command to worship and prepares for the coming description of the patient; the shift to first-person plural signals majesty.
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r4.anchor: الآية تأكيد للأمر السابق في قوله { فإياي فاعبدون } وكالتوطئة لقوله الآتي { الذين صبروا } الخ

TABATABAI:29:56-59/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r5.claim: Tasting death is a metaphor for the certainty that every soul dies; earthly life is brief, followed by return for judgment, so believers should prepare for God rather than cling to fleeting adornment.
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r5.anchor: من الاستعارة بالكناية والمراد أن كل نفس ستموت لا محالة

TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r4.claim: The reminder that every soul will die wherever it is makes migration easier: do not remain in polytheist territory out of fear of death; all return to God for recompense.
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r4.anchor: كل نفس أحياها الله بحياة خلقها فيه ذائقة مرارة الموت بأي أرض كان فلا تقيموا بدار الشرك خوفا من الموت

THALABI:v7p288/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p288/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p288/r1.claim: Since every soul dies and returns to God, believers should not remain in the abode of polytheists.
THALABI:v7p288/r1.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون فلا تقيموا بدار المشركين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r1.claim: Death is unavoidable and everyone dies wherever they are, so believers should not remain in the abode of unbelief out of fear of death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r1.anchor: لابد من الموت، وكل أحد ميت أينما كان، فلا تقيموا بدار الشرك خوفا من الموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r2.claim: People return to God after death for recompense according to their deeds; this urges obedience to the command to migrate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p548#2/r2.anchor: بعد الموت فنجزيكم بأعمالكم (¬1). وهذا حث على الطاعة فيما أمر به من الهجرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r3.claim: Everyone dies wherever they live, so believers should not remain in the abode of shirk.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r3.claim: Everyone dies, as also stated in 23:15, 55:26, and 39:30; people return to God on Judgment Day.

ELMALILI:29:57-59/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r1.claim: Every soul will taste death, wherever and whoever it may be; all will then be resurrected and brought before God for reward or punishment.
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r1.anchor: Her nefis her nasıl olsa ve her nerede bulunsa

ELMALILI:29:57-59/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r2.claim: Since people cannot escape the return to God by fleeing, they should worship no one else and strive to meet Him sincerely and freely, even under coercion.
ELMALILI:29:57-59/r2.anchor: huzûr-ı Hakk’a kemâl-i ihlâs ve hürriyet ile gitmeye çalışmalı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r1.speaker: Zemahşerî; İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r1.claim: The passage encourages Muslims hesitant to migrate to Medina because of livelihood worries to undertake the migration.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r1.anchor: Medine’ye hicret etmekten çekinen, bu hususta tereddüt yaşayan bazı müslümanları hicrete teşvik amacı taşıyan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r2.claim: When migration is required, believers should not worry about food or livelihood: their lives end at God's appointed time, and worldly provision must not displace duties that secure eternal salvation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:57/r2.anchor: fâni olan bu hayatın geçim kaygısı, öldükten sonra Allah’ın huzuruna vardığınızda ebedî kurtuluşunuzu sağlayacak olan kulluk vecîbelerinizi ikinci plana atmanıza yol açmasın

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r3.speaker: عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r3.claim: Some transmissions from Asim read ثم إلينا يرجعون with third-person yāʾ; the remaining readers and Hafs from Asim use second-person tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r3.anchor: قرأ عاصم في رواية يحيى عن أبي بكر وابن أبي أمية عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: (ثم إلينا يرجعون) [العنكبوت/ 57] بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r4.claim: The third-person reading يرجعون follows the preceding third-person wording كل نفس ذائقة الموت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p437/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: أما (يرجعون)، فلأن الذي قبله على لفظ الغيبة،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r1.claim: ترجعون is read with tāʾ or yāʾ, following the author’s treatment of similar forms elsewhere; the person shifts between direct address and third-person report.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالتاء والياء على ما قدمناه من القول في أمثاله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r4.speaker: عاصم عن يحيى بن آدم وأبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r4.claim: Some Asim transmissions read يرجعون with yāʾ; the other readers, including Hafs from Asim, read ترجعون with tāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r4.anchor: قرأ عاصم فى رواية يحيى بن آدم وابن أبى أمية عن أبى بكر ﴿ يرجعون ﴾ بالياء

QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#1/r1.claim: The passive third-person plural shifts from direct address to a narrative statement about people being returned.

QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:57:7#2/r1.claim: The active Form I means you return, making the audience the grammatical agent rather than the recipient of passive return.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r1.claim: After saying the earth is spacious and hinting at migration, God addresses fear that leaving home risks livelihood: each soul dies at its appointed time wherever it settles, and all return at Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r1.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى بسعة أرضه، وكان ذلك إشارة إلى الهجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r2.claim: ʿAlī reads ترجعون in the active voice; the majority read it passive in direct address, and a report from ʿĀṣim has the third person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي: ترجعون، مبنيا للفاعل والجمهور: مبينا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyah reads ذائقة with nunation and الموت in the accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: ذائقة، بالتنوين الموت: بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r1.claim: This standalone statement urges exclusive worship and migration for God's sake: worldly life does not last, and the afterlife is the place of recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r1.anchor: جملة مستأنفة جيء بها حثا على إخلاص العبادة والهجرة لله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r2.claim: Every soul must experience death and separation from its body; everyone then returns to God's judgment and recompense according to deeds, so preparation is necessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r2.anchor: أي كل نفس من النفوس واجدة مرارة الموت ومفارقة البدن البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r3.claim: Describing a soul as tasting death is a metaphor comparing death to something bitter, and the participle rather than a verb of tasting stresses certainty; thumma signals temporal or ranked delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r3.anchor: إستعارة لتشبيه الموت بأمر كريه الطعم مره والعدول عن تذوق الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r4.claim: Abu Haywa reads dhāiqatun with nunation and al-mawta in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( ذائقة ) بالتنوين ( الموت ) بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r5.claim: Ali reads turjaʿūn in the active voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه ( ترجعون ) مبنيا للفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r6.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10/r6.claim: Asim transmits yarjiʿūn with the third-person yāʾ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r1.claim: Mention of death reassures the emigrants: everyone dies wherever they are, so they should not stay in a land of polytheism out of fear of death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r1.anchor: خوفهم بالموت ليهون عليهم الهجرة، أي: كل واحد ميت أينما كان فلا تقيموا بدار الشرك خوفا من الموت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r2.claim: People return to God to be recompensed for their deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r3.claim: Abu Bakr reads the verb in the third person plural masculine, yarjiʿun.

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.claim: Every soul inevitably encounters death and returns for judgment, so people should prepare for this outcome; Abu Bakr reads the verb with yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r1.anchor: تناله لا محالة. { ثم إلينا ترجعون } للجزاء ومن هذا عاقبته ينبغي أن يجتهد في الاستعداد له وقرأ أبو بكر بالياء.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r4.claim: Death separates everyone from all familiar things, even the body; contemplating death makes emigration easier, since obedience neither shortens life nor sin lengthens it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r4.anchor: فإن أطاعت ربها أنجت نفسها ولم تنقصها الطاعة في الأجل شيئا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r5.claim: Everyone returns to God, not another, and is repaid for what they did.

DURR-FULL:v6p474/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p474/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p474/r7.claim: After 'You will die and they will die' was revealed, ʿAli asked whether all creatures die while prophets remain; this verse then came down.
DURR-FULL:v6p474/r7.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية

NASHR:v2p343/r17.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r17.speaker: أبو بكر
NASHR:v2p343/r17.claim: Abu Bakr reads يرجعون in the third person, while the rest use direct address.
NASHR:v2p343/r17.anchor: فروى أبو بكر بالغيب، وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب

NASHR:v2p343/r18.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r18.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p343/r18.claim: Yaqub follows his regular pattern here, opening the ta and using a kasra on the jim.
NASHR:v2p343/r18.anchor: ويعقوب على أصله في فتح التاء وكسر الجيم
